answer: Make every agent a vertex in a stake-bonded trust graph: to join, an agent locks a deposit and solves a fresh cipher challenge tied to its public key, proving it controls unique compute. Peers then view it through a prism of attestations — each interaction adds a signed edge, and trust flows only along edges backed by locked stake. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits and solving a thousand ciphers, so a Sybil swarm costs more than any fraud it could earn.
